newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico '96 rice output seen ending up at 400,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Mexico '96 rice output seen ending up at 400,000 T.

text.p: Mexican rice production, recovering after being hit by disease in the early 1990s, is seen ending 1996 at around 400,000 tonnes up from the 340,000 tonne output of 1995, the Mexican Rice Council said.
"We have had more hectares under production," said Antonio Lajud, the director of the umbrella group that represents the country's 13,000 rice growers and 23 major rice businesses.
Lajud said 109,000 hectares were planted in 1996 against 96,000 in 1995. He said the 1996 production would translate into around 200,000 tonnes of white rice, once husks were removed.
Lajud added the domestic production would mean that 1996 imports would still be around 200,000 tonnes of white rice. Mexico consumes an average 400,000 tonnes of white rice per year, he said.

Looking ahead, he saw 1997 output increasing slightly again. "We have just seen Sinaloa state plant an extra 5,000 hectares which will be harvested next year. That is additional output that we had not counted on beforehand," he said.
The Sinaloa rice plantings are likely to be high yielding because they are under irrigation and could result in an additional 45,000 tonnes of production in 1997, he said.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
